title: Pinned real Ribasim saveat negative control without management scarcity

sequencing.rationale: Freeze the causal negative control before observing the saveat sweep.

purpose: Test whether saveat sensitivity requires state-dependent management reallocation. Remove management scarcity while retaining the same physical min_level reduction and saveat sweep.

independent_continuous_reference.ode: A dh/dtau = 60 * (1 - phi(h-0.99)), tau in days. Allocation is demand-capped at 40/20 m3/day at every solve, so repeated optimization cannot change the physical target.
independent_continuous_reference.ledger: 60 m3 fixed inflow = total physical UserDemand supply + Basin storage gain.

hypotheses: All saveat cases allocate the full 40/20 m3/day demand from the first management solve onward.
Repeated saveat-synchronized allocation solves therefore do not alter allocated targets.
Physical supplied volumes, Basin trajectory and final level are invariant across 1h, 6h, 12h and 24h saveat within tolerance.
If DUMMY-19G shows saveat sensitivity while DUMMY-19H does not, the causal mechanism is management reoptimization of retained storage rather than the physical output-saving operation itself.
forbidden: no post-output change to source supply, demands, saveat sweep, references or tolerances
no claim that this resolves the upstream clock-design limitation

authority_rebind.meaning: Executable implementation is rebound after 19G closeout; the frozen no-scarcity model, saveat sweep, references and tolerances are unchanged.
